encoder_inventory.scope: Original MT_PLAYER0 and MT_SERGEANT12, fixed active player0. Source player/mo/roster rows and ordered Look/Chase/attack/damage events independently encode unchanged DSIM22 fields with policy6 and a distinct melee context. Command gate plus original thinkers is not full P_Ticker/PlayerThink/DeathThink. Birth/generation projection remains separate Rust schema policy. No Rust expected outputs.

performance.method: Matching Rust1.99.1 release tools/workloads, three timing/RSS and three allocation processes per group. No concurrent local fuzz/test load. Shared host is not isolated. New melee groups are separate from historical comparisons. Warmup, controlled initial health/impulse and final explicit capture are excluded from intervals, included in whole-process RSS.

development_corrections: Only the new boundary source input was moved inside the unchanged travel-envelope proof before expectations were committed. No historical fixture or runtime bound changed.

Execution capability belongs to PlayerRuntime, not OriginalPlayer. A transient action selector carries that existing immutable capability; no persistent duplicate policy/identity field was introduced.
Fuzz operation error types were normalized for comparison without changing public runtime errors or gameplay behavior.
source_limits: One genuine player0 with fixed active roster and at most one map-THING MT_SERGEANT; supported grounded static geometry.
Bounded original-source command/reaction conditional before actual thinkers, not full PlayerThink/Ticker/DeathThink.
Current staged range/health/position and actual late RNG feed the shared DamagePlan. Errors discard existing transaction.
Reverse thrust is unreachable for both grounded actors; extreme autonomous player death is unreachable for source4..40 damage starting at positive health.
New turns are nonnegative literal-defined cases. Reused negative-turn bit interpretation is not portable ISO-C equivalence for signed-shift UB.
Rust retirement/generation/provenance protections are separate from original pointer behavior. No new C freed-memory or allocator-reuse observations.
